title: Shemirat Halashon 29

chapters.title: Exceptions to Speaking Before Three People
chapters.about: Rules for a person known strictly for truthfulness when communicating for To'elet

chapters.title: Interpersonal Sins vs. Sins Against God
chapters.about: Why constructive speech applies to interpersonal harms rather than private sins against God

chapters.title: Personal Grievances and Seeking Revenge
chapters.about: The danger of personal bias and retribution when reporting harm done to oneself

chapters.title: Refusing Favors and Criticizing Communities
chapters.about: Prohibition of speaking ill of individuals or entire towns for lacking hospitality

chapters.title: Informing People of Influence for Protection
chapters.about: When it is permitted to inform someone who can rectify harm or stop future damage

chapters.title: Firsthand Knowledge and Avoiding Bias
chapters.about: Requirements of direct evidence, careful judgment, and overcoming self-justification

summary: This class continues the study of Hafes Hayim, Hilkhot Lashon HaRa chapter 10, exploring the precise conditions under which negative information may be shared for a constructive benefit (To'elet). It analyzes the distinction between sins committed between man and God versus those between man and his fellow, as well as the rules governing a person known for truthfulness. Additionally, the class addresses the grave caution required when discussing personal grievances, warning against revenge and personal bias.
subjects: B'Ape Telata (in front of three people)
Ben Adam L'Havero vs. Ben Adam L'Makom
Speaking ill of a city or community
questions: Does a person known for absolute truthfulness need to report harmful behavior in front of three people?
May one publicize sins that are strictly between man and God for a constructive purpose?
What precautions must a person take when speaking about harm done directly to themselves?
Is it permitted to complain about a community or host that did not show hospitality?
When is it allowed to tell a figure of authority or influence about another person's wrongdoing?
